statement: An explicit owner approval for a named piece counts whether the owner gives it on the board or types it in a working session. Work on that piece is not held waiting for a board click; the session reconciles the board record to the typed approval. Approval still covers only the named piece and action, and assistant text, inference or silence never counts as approval.
conditions: Applies to approval gates in the content-engine board and production flow.
The approval must be the owner's own typed words naming the piece or action, not an assistant summary.
Any external publish, send or spend still needs explicit approval immediately before that action under the canon.
uncertainties: The ruling line was written into the commit by an assistant session, so its wording is a recorded paraphrase plus a quoted owner remark.
The cause of the board being out of date has not been diagnosed, so how the board should be repaired is open.
Whether a typed approval should also stamp the board automatically or only by the session is undecided.
why: The owner corrected sessions that refused to proceed until the board approve control was pressed, saying approval counts wherever given and that the board is not pressed because it is stale. The owning defect is board freshness and a gate that reads only one channel, so the procedure should make the gate accept both channels and keep the board reconciled rather than adding a separate taste rule.
alternative_explanations: The remark may reflect frustration with one stale period of the board rather than a permanent preference; once the board is reliable the owner might again want the board to be the single record. It might also apply only to internal production steps and not to the final publish slot.
if_wrong: Sessions could act on a loosely worded chat remark as approval, or the board could lose its role as the record of what was approved. The owner would notice a piece moving forward that was not clearly approved, or a board that no longer matches what shipped.
validation: A board regression case where an owner typed approval exists for a named piece but the board still shows pending: the session proceeds and updates the board, while a case with only assistant text or silence stays blocked. Track whether owner corrections about stalled approvals stop recurring.
rollback: Mark this record superseded or revert the review merge, restoring board approval as the only recognised channel; no evidence is erased and the board itself is untouched.
